text:
mari-plat: Quick design thread — migrate billing_metrics.route_id from text -> bigint via tenant-scoped rollout. Route values are numeric fingerprints ~98% of rows so perf wins look promising.

sophia: Agree on perf. Main concerns: backfill IO, index bloat, dashboard compatibility.

anil: Proposed approach: add route_id_int NULL + migration_status; enable dual-write behind feature flag; reads go through adapter preferring int when present. Backfill per-tenant windows with rate limits and a migration control table.

gabe: Important: billing batch jobs and S3 export must read via the adapter to avoid divergence. I'll update those pipelines.

jess: QA plan: two canary tenants that mirror heavy load. Compare aggregates pre/post migration; tolerance 0.01%.

sre-oncall: Runbook: schema add during low-traffic (Fri 02:00 UTC), throttled backfill, alert if fallback_reads_pct > 1% or backfill_error_rate > 0.5%. Rollback: disable dual-write + point reads to text.

mari-plat: Indexing: create CONCURRENT index on route_id_int after tenant marked done, then drop text index and column after safety window (60-90d). Consider partial indexes for top tenants to reduce bloat.

anil: For very large tenants we may use copy-to-new-table pattern instead of row-by-row UPDATEs. Tradeoffs: extra storage and complexity.

sophia: Console UX: show "legacy id" badge when route_id_int is null; expose admin view for migration_status per-tenant.

jess: Telemetry: add backfill_rows/sec, fallback_reads_pct, avg_query_ms_by_column and dashboards before starting.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: billing-ingest-v3 -> canary-pool at 2026-03-23T02:00:00Z.

mari-plat: I'll open PRs: schema + dual-write flag, read adapter changes, backfill orchestrator, migration control table, dashboards, and the runbook. Volunteers: anil owns orchestration, sophia owns console changes, gabe owns batch/export updates.

sophia: Sounds good — post runbook link here when ready and we can lock dates.
